pages.title: RedLink Support
pages.description: Get help with RedLink, the unofficial Toyota companion maintained by Oliver Ames, and find its privacy and data controls.
pages.body_html:
RedLink Support

I'm Oliver Ames, and I maintain RedLink, an unofficial companion for vehicles connected to Toyota North America accounts. For help with the app, email oliver@ames.consulting.

RedLink isn't affiliated with or endorsed by Toyota. The features available to you depend on your vehicle and the connected services available to your Toyota account.

Report a problem

Include your RedLink version and build, device and operating system, vehicle model and year, and the steps that led to the problem. Tell me whether it happened in the app, on Apple Watch, in a widget or through another control.

Don't send your Toyota password, verification code or full VIN. If you choose to share a diagnostic log, review it first because it can contain vehicle readings and other personal information. In development and TestFlight builds, you can prepare a log in Settings > Developer Tools > Diagnostic Logs.

Check vehicle status and controls

Compare the last server check with the time your vehicle last reported. A successful request doesn't always mean the vehicle has completed a command, and background updates depend on iOS scheduling. Use vehicle controls only when you can safely verify the result.

Auto-lock is optional and uses reported lock and activity information. It doesn't detect key proximity, so don't rely on it as a guarantee that the vehicle is locked.

For help with your Toyota account or connected-service access, use Toyota Support.

Manage your data

In Settings > Data & History, you can choose a history period and use Clear All Trend History to remove saved trends for all accounts and vehicles. Signing out clears the saved Toyota session and vehicle cache, but it doesn't erase trend archives or diagnostic logs.

Watch sync is controlled in Settings > Apple Watch. Disabling it removes synced account and vehicle information when the removal reaches the Watch.

Read the RedLink Privacy Policy for details about account information, local storage, Watch sync and support messages. For a privacy question or to request deletion of support emails or logs you've sent me, email oliver@ames.consulting.

pages.title: RedLink Privacy Policy
pages.description: How RedLink handles Toyota account information, vehicle data, Apple Watch sync, local history, diagnostic logs and support requests.
pages.body_html:
RedLink Privacy Policy

Effective October 8, 2026.

RedLink is maintained by Oliver Ames. It's an unofficial companion for vehicles connected to Toyota North America accounts and isn't affiliated with or endorsed by Toyota. This policy describes how the app handles account information, vehicle data and diagnostic logs, and how I handle support emails and logs you send me.

Connecting your Toyota account

When you sign in, RedLink sends your username, password and any requested verification code to Toyota's sign-in service. The app saves the resulting session tokens, account and device identifiers, username and selected vehicle identifier so it can retrieve vehicle information and send the commands you request.

The saved session doesn't include your password. RedLink clears the password and verification-code input after a successful sign-in and when you sign out.

RedLink communicates directly with Toyota's account and connected-services endpoints. Toyota describes its handling of your account and connected-service data in its Connected Services Privacy Notice.

Vehicle information on your Apple devices

Depending on your vehicle and connected services, RedLink receives and saves information such as the VIN, vehicle name and model, owner name, reported vehicle location, fuel or charge level, odometer, tire pressures, door and window status, climate status, supported features and vehicle reports. These readings populate vehicle status and controls and provide the samples used in Trends.

RedLink stores session and vehicle information in a shared Apple keychain used by the app and its extensions. It also saves preferences and local files on your device. Widgets, Live Activities, Siri, Shortcuts and Spotlight use saved vehicle information. Vehicle images may load from image URLs supplied with the vehicle data.

Sync with Apple Watch is enabled by default. It sends the Toyota session and selected vehicle information to your paired Watch through Apple's WatchConnectivity framework. You can turn it off in Settings > Apple Watch. Turning it off removes the synced account and vehicle information when the removal reaches the Watch.

History and deletion controls

Trends records locally saved vehicle readings. The default history period is 30 days, and you can choose 30, 60 or 120 days in Settings > Data & History. RedLink applies retention and reduces the detail of older samples when it updates history, so older files can remain while the app is inactive.

Clear All Trend History removes locally saved trend history for all accounts and vehicles. Signing out clears the saved session, vehicle snapshot and vehicle list and sends a removal to your paired Watch. It doesn't erase trend archives or diagnostic logs. A disconnected Watch may receive the removal later.

Diagnostic logs and sharing

RedLink keeps local diagnostic logs to help investigate failures. Logs can include the app version, events, timestamps, request status, error details and selected vehicle readings. The app limits the log size and trims older entries as new entries are written.

The logger masks credential-like fields and identifier patterns, but a logged VIN can retain its last four characters. Logs can also retain the vehicle model, model year and telemetry. Treat a diagnostic log as potentially personal information.

In development and TestFlight builds, you can prepare a log in Settings > Developer Tools > Diagnostic Logs and choose whether to share it. Review the file before sending it. Sharing creates a copy for the destination you select, and clearing local app data doesn't delete a copy you've already sent.

Support emails and logs you send me

If you email oliver@ames.consulting, I receive your email address, message and any attachments you choose to include. I use that information to respond to your request and investigate the problem. Email services process and store the messages used for that correspondence.

I keep support emails and the diagnostic logs you send me until I delete them or receive a request from you to delete them. To make a deletion request, email me at the address above and identify the correspondence or logs you'd like deleted. This request concerns the support material you've sent me; Toyota handles its account and connected-service records separately.

When you test RedLink through TestFlight, Apple automatically collects crash logs and usage information and shares them with me as the developer. Apple also shares feedback you submit, and some information may be associated with your name and email address. Apple's TestFlight privacy information describes the data, invitation-dependent differences and Apple's retention practices.

Contact

For RedLink support, privacy questions or deletion requests, contact Oliver Ames at oliver@ames.consulting. You can also visit the RedLink support page.
